LEAID=3307360 | Pinkerton Academy School District, NEW HAMPSHIRE | Step 1
============================================================
**Dr. Timothy J. Powers is the Head of School (top leader) for Pinkerton Academy School District for the 2025–2026 school year.[4][2]**

## Governance Structure
Pinkerton Academy operates as an independent academy serving multiple NH towns (Derry, Chester, Hampstead, etc.), governed by a Board of Trustees rather than a traditional superintendent.[1] The Head of School supervises overall school operations under the Board's direction, fitting the query's allowance for the top leader in a single-school district.[1][1][2]

## Confirmation Details
The district's official administration page lists Dr. Timothy J. Powers as Head of School with credentials (Ed.D., Walden University) and contact info, current as of 2025–2026.[2] The Board of Trustees page for 2025–2026 confirms this structure with no superintendent named; external sources like NHIAA also reference him as Head of School.[1][10][1]

LEAID=5002610 | Brighton School District, VERMONT | Step 1
============================================================
Based on my research, I have found clear and authoritative information about the superintendent for Brighton School District.

**Elaine Collins is the superintendent of North Country Supervisory Union (NCSU), which oversees Brighton School District in Island Pond, Vermont, for the 2025–2026 school year.** [7][8]

## District Structure

Brighton School District is a component of the North Country Supervisory Union, as noted in the query. [5] In Vermont's supervisory union structure, the superintendent of the supervisory union serves as the chief educational officer for the member districts, including Brighton School District. Elaine Collins has served as superintendent of NCSU since at least 2023, making her third year in the role as of March 2025. [8]

## School Leadership

Brighton Elementary School (the primary school in Brighton School District serving Island Pond) is led by Principal Annsunee Swift. [7]

============================================================
**As of February 27, 2026, Dr. Stuart Blount is the acting superintendent of Craven County Schools (Craven County Board of Education), serving in an interim capacity during the transition to the permanent superintendent, Dr. Matthew Cheeseman.[1][5]**

## Leadership Timeline
Dr. Wendy Miller resigned effective May 30, 2025, after which Richard L. Stout, Jr. became interim superintendent starting May 1, 2025.[4][5][14]  
Dr. Stuart Blount was then appointed interim superintendent effective January 1, 2026, to ensure leadership continuity until Dr. Cheeseman's official start.[1][5]  
Dr. Matthew Cheeseman was unanimously approved as the new permanent superintendent on December 16, 2025, took his oath on January 12, 2026, but does not begin serving until February 1, 2026.[1][6][7]

## District Website Status
The official site (cravenk12.org) still highlights earlier interim announcements like Stout's but lacks an update confirming Cheeseman's active role as of the latest fetch, consistent with his future start date.[1][14]

LEAID=0625150 | Modesto City High, CALIFORNIA | Step 1
============================================================
Based on my research, I have found clear information about the superintendent of Modesto City Schools for the 2025–2026 school year.

**Dr. Vanessa Buitrago is the Superintendent of Modesto City Schools for the 2025–2026 school year.** [1][2][10] She was appointed by the Board of Education on May 12, 2025, and officially assumed the role on July 1, 2025. [1]

## Background

Dr. Buitrago is a graduate of Modesto City Schools, having attended Elihu Beard Elementary, Roosevelt Junior High, and Modesto High School (graduating in 2001 as an International Baccalaureate student). [1] She brings over 20 years of experience in education and educational leadership, including roles as a teacher, principal, and assistant superintendent in Sacramento City Unified School District, as well as a network deputy superintendent at Oakland Unified School District. [1]

## Transition Details

Dr. Buitrago succeeded retiring Superintendent Dr. Sara Noguchi, who ended her tenure at the conclusion of the 2024–2025 academic year. [1][12] The Board of Education conducted an extensive search process with 14 applicants and selected Buitrago following interviews and input from parents, students, and educational partners. [1]

============================================================
Based on my research, I have found clear information about the leadership structure of The Catamount School for the 2025–2026 school year.

The Catamount School is a laboratory school operated by Western Carolina University in partnership with Jackson County Public Schools. [10] **Kim Winter**, Dean of WCU's College of Education and Allied Professions, serves as **superintendent for TCS** [10], making her the top leader of the school. [10] Sarah Tatham serves as Principal. [10]

However, there is structural ambiguity regarding whether Kim Winter's position as superintendent is held in her university role (Dean) or in a primary K-12 leadership capacity. According to your guidance, individuals whose primary roles include "Dean" of a university college should be excluded if their title is primarily university-based. Winter is listed as "dean of WCU's College of Education and Allied Professions and superintendent for TCS," indicating her superintendent title is secondary to her university dean role. [10]

Given this ambiguity, **Sarah Tatham**, whose primary title is **Principal of The Catamount School**, is the most appropriate answer as the top K-12 leader whose role is dedicated to leading the school itself. [9][10]

Rochester Stockbridge Unified School District is part of the White River Valley Supervisory Union (WRVSU), and the supervisory union's superintendent serves all component districts, including Rochester Stockbridge Unified. [1][13]

**Jamie Kinnarney** is the Superintendent of Schools for the White River Valley Supervisory Union and therefore serves Rochester Stockbridge Unified School District. [13][4] This is confirmed by multiple recent sources, including a YouTube recording from May 12, 2025 (the RSUD annual reorganization meeting) where Kinnarney is identified as "the superintendent of schools," [4] and official legislative testimony from January 2026 confirming the role. [10]

The district website lists community letters from Superintendent Jamie Kinnarney for the 2025-2026 school year, further confirming current service in this role. [13]

LEAID=3413890 | River Edge School District, NEW JERSEY | Step 1
============================================================
**Dr. Nicholas A. Bernice is the superintendent of River Edge School District in New Jersey for the 2025–2026 school year.** [1][13]

## Appointment Details
Dr. Bernice was appointed by the River Edge Board of Education, starting July 1, 2024, following a comprehensive search.[1][1] Previously the 2024 New Jersey Superintendent of the Year from Ringwood Public Schools, he now leads as the top educational official.[1]

## Current Confirmation
District staff listings and the superintendent's office page confirm him in the role.[2][5] State records from 2023–2024 and a January 2025 financial report list Dr. Nicholas Bernice as superintendent.[13][16] A February 2026 source also identifies him as superintendent, discussing ongoing board activities like NJSLA results and budgets.[9]

## Earlier Context
Prior acting superintendent Lisa Bernardo served before his appointment, noted in older records, but no evidence shows departure during 2025–2026.[4][7]

============================================================
**Matthew D. Webb is the superintendent of the Lenape Regional High School District for the 2025–2026 school year.** [1][7][1]

## Leadership Transition
The Lenape Regional High School District (LRHSD) Board of Education unanimously approved Matthew Webb, previously the assistant superintendent, as the new superintendent on July 23, 2025, effective September 1, 2025, succeeding Dr. Carol Birnbohm upon her retirement. [1][1] This change occurred before the 2025–2026 school year (August 2025–June 2026), and district administration pages list Webb in the role as of October 2025. [7][1]

## Confirmation
District board highlights from January 2026 do not indicate any further changes, supporting Webb's ongoing service. [2] Older documents like the 2025-2026 student handbook list Birnbohm but predate the transition. [5]

============================================================
**David Baker is the superintendent of the Orleans Southwest Supervisory Union, which oversees the Mountain View Union Elementary School District #94 as a component district.[6][2]**

## Leadership Structure
Mountain View Union Elementary School District #94 (Hardwick, VT) is a component of the Orleans Southwest Supervisory Union (OSSU), and Vermont supervisory unions provide centralized leadership including the superintendent for their member districts.[6][8] David Baker serves as OSSU Superintendent, referenced in current district resources and state records for the 2025-26 school year.[1][1] No separate superintendent is listed for MVU itself; school-level leaders include principals like William Deiss (Hardwick Elementary).[2]

## Recent Confirmation
Vermont Agency of Education records list David Baker as OSSU Superintendent as of January 28, 2025.[2] A February 2025 news article confirms Baker sharing updates on MVU matters, indicating ongoing service.[8] District staff pages and newsletters also name Dr. David Baker as Superintendent.[1]

**Shauna Schmerer is the superintendent of Bandon SD 54 for the 2025–2026 school year.** [1][2][4]

## Leadership Confirmation
The official district website lists Shauna Schmerer as Superintendent and Homeless Liaison/Civil Rights Coordinator, with her contact email sschmerer@bandon.k12.or.us, alongside other administrators like principals and directors. [1][2][4] This appears on both the homepage and dedicated administration page, indicating current status as of February 2026. [1][2]

## Recent Developments
News from December 2025 and January 2026 reports ongoing complaints and investigations into Schmerer, including a contract amendment approved by the board and hiring of a private investigator, but no removal, resignation, or replacement. [1][3][17] A February 2026 article notes the board dismissing further complaints against her, confirming she remains in the role. [10] Earlier sites listing "Doug Ardiana" as superintendent appear outdated or erroneous, as current district pages and 2025-2026 news consistently name Schmerer. [8]
